chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn al-Jahm narrated from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the person in iʿtikaf who approaches his family. He said: “He must not approach his wife, neither by night nor by day, while he is in iʿtikaf.”

key_terms.أَهْلَهُ: his family, here referring to his wife
key_terms.الْمُعْتَكِفِ: the person observing iʿtikaf, a spiritual retreat in worship
key_terms.مُعْتَكِفٌ: one who is presently in the state of iʿtikaf
key_terms.يَأْتِي: approaches sexually or engages in conjugal relations

ai.seo_question: Can a person in iʿtikaf have relations with their spouse at night or during the day?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning iʿtikaf, stating that one in retreat must abstain from conjugal relations throughout the entire period, both night and day. It highlights the sanctity and devotional focus of iʿtikaf in Shia fiqh.
